quests.title: Cupid's Lover

dialogue.t: Someone was just here! Paimon can't believe we've run into someone with better archaeological exploration chops than us.
Is that... a pocket watch on the ground?
If this is anything like our usual adventures, we should take a look at this stone tablet.
"Lo, this place is the Orthant of Souls, the Shrine of Souls, the Room of Souls..."
"I accompany you in eternal rest"... "Born in an instant, often contradicting, always united"... "I am life's most cherished treasure"...
Hmmm... A valuable pocket watch, and one of life's treasures...
Ooh, Paimon knows! It's gotta be Mora!
You're right, the answer to a riddle wouldn't be so tacky. Then it must be... What's the word...
Right, "wealth"!

dialogue.sit: Wonderful, that's one answer we can count out.

dialogue.t: Come on! Why can't you just trust Paimon?
Well, if you're so smart, what do you think it is?

dialogue.sit: It's not important. Let's go in deeper and take a look around.

dialogue.t: Hey! Don't change the subject.
"Lo, this place is the Orthant of Souls, the Shrine of Souls, the Room of Souls..."
"I accompany you in eternal rest"... "Born in an instant, often contradicting, always united"... "I am life's most cherished treasure"...
Phew... Nothing scary this time. Is the answer a pocket watch?
Speaking of which, don't you have one too, Ann?
Then the answer must be money, as in Mora!
Passing away along with your money is life's second-greatest tragedy. Don't ask what the greatest one is.
What is life's greatest tragedy then?
I am aware of this one. It is "to rest in your coffin without a single Mora to your name."
I'm not sure I agree with those values. Aren't there many things more important than that?
Well, that's why I said "don't ask."
I apologize.
Anyway, based on the above reasons, I don't think the answer is a fancy timepiece, nor is it Mora.
What could it be, then?
The answer is simple — I can retrieve similar riddles with a 70% match rate.
This is from a centuries-old classic novel. It reads, "I was born in the fleeting moment when eyes meet. I run with my back turned to the one I pursue."
"Even after all flesh, bone, and entrails have been sliced away, I still lie nestled with you in the marrow that remains."
The answer is "love."
I get it now. This pocket watch is just like the one I have, then — It must be filled with memories of love.

dialogue.sit: Now, if only it would open.

dialogue.t: It will, one day.
Why, well done, you silly dog! Who's the cutest mechanical dog?
It was my pleasure. "Cute," however, is a subjective description. I would prefer to be addressed as "the reliable, useful Prototype 4ACV07."
And that's exactly what makes you so cute.
Are you reenacting an old conversation? I feel like I've seen this scene before.
In any case, someone's already solved this riddle. Let's get moving.

dialogue.sit: You carefully inspect the top of the mechanism, but you don't find anything.

dialogue.t: There's nothing here?
Oh no! It looks like someone already took whatever was here.
But who?

dialogue.sit: You carefully inspect the top of the mechanism, but you don't find anything.

dialogue.t: There's nothing here either...

dialogue.sit: You carefully inspect the top of the mechanism, but you don't find anything.

dialogue.t: Did someone... take whatever was here, too?

dialogue.sit: You carefully inspect the top of the mechanism, but you don't find anything.

dialogue.t: There's nothing here?
It looks like something was here, but someone else took it.
Wait, doesn't that mean that our plan's already failed?
The birth of "reason" requires the merging of the four orthants. If we can get the rest of them, we still have a chance.
In that case, we'd better hurry to the next area.

dialogue.sit: You carefully inspect the top of the mechanism, but you don't find anything.

dialogue.t: There's nothing here either...
What exactly are we looking for, Caterpillar?
We're looking for the materials necessary to forge the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz.
The Ordo was able to reproduce the four requisite hypothetical substances here in the material world, based on the esoteric philosophies of the underground kingdom and ancient Fontaine.
I do not understand.
These enigmatic substances are purely experiential. You could say they are even further beyond ordinary logic than elemental power.
I entered all introductory to intermediate level textbooks from the Akademiya's Spantamad into my memory banks decades ago. There is nothing mysterious about elemental power.
Is that so? Anyway, to sum up, this is born of the confluence of traditions from Fontaine and technology from the ancient underground kingdom.
And thus, four types of substance came into being: Memory, Wish, Soul, and Persona.
To avoid any possible ambiguity, let's call them the "Memory" piece, "Wish" piece, "Soul" piece, and "Persona" piece.
Why are these used to make the Holy Blade?
In the Narzissenkreuz Ordo's brand of mystical philosophy, the temple is a microcosm of the universe, the members are stand-ins for the gods, and the holy oil is tempered willpower.
The Holy Blade, on the other hand, is "reason," that which cuts everything open. It can only be born out of consummate human will.
That's esotericism for you. You attach yourself to anything that looks similar enough, and when this sort of thing becomes magic, fiction becomes reality.
Anyway, we should make our way to the next area now.

dialogue.sit: You carefully inspect the top of the mechanism, but you don't find anything.

dialogue.t: Did someone... take whatever was here, too?
Looks that way.
It's Jakob.
We had an altercation with him inside Elynas once... Clarification: Recently, not "once."
When I saw that unfortunate victim at the gate, I knew it was his handiwork. It seems he's still active after all.
Then what does he want with the stuff he took from here?
Simple — He too wants to reforge the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz. The dream of the Ordo remains unrealized.
Anyway, we should make our way to the final area now.

quests.description: Trace and find the Narzissenkreuz Ordo’s seals.
